name: OpenHands (Agent Canvas)

runner.notes: Prefer the Docker sandbox path for parity: mount the parent of runs/<run-id>/worktree as PROJECTS_PATH and run ghcr.io/openhands/agent-canvas:<version> (UI at http://localhost:8000/canvas), or `npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas && agent-canvas` (Node 24+, uv; no sandbox, host filesystem access). Configure the LLM (BYO key) or pick an ACP agent (Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI) in Settings -> Agent, open only the task worktree as the workspace, paste prompt.md into a new conversation, then harness-verify on the worktree. Record Agent Canvas version (e.g. 1.24.0), agent (OpenHands vs ACP guest), LLM/model, backend (local process vs Docker vs Cloud), and interventions. Do not mix OpenHands Cloud runs into local Class A results without caveat.

inclusion: Class A self-hostable local ADE: the MIT OpenHands repo now ships Agent Canvas, a local-first control center (web UI via npm/Docker plus preview Electron desktop packages) for conversations, terminals, files, and scheduled/webhook automations across local, Docker, VM, Kubernetes, and cloud agent backends. It runs its own OpenHands Software Agent SDK agent out of the box and also drives guest ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, custom), so runtime_model is hybrid. OpenHands Cloud/Enterprise are commercial add-ons and are not the benchmark surface.
runtime_model_notes: Default agent is the first-party OpenHands agent from the MIT Software Agent SDK (BYO LLM via LiteLLM-backed provider-agnostic interface); Agent Canvas can switch to ACP guest agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI presets or any stdio ACP server).
pricing_model: Open source Agent Canvas / SDK are MIT and free with BYO LLM key. OpenHands Cloud Individual is free to start (10 daily conversations, BYO key or OpenHands LLM provider at cost, Jira/Slack integrations). Enterprise (SaaS or self-hosted VPC) is commercially licensed with custom pricing (SAML/SSO, unlimited concurrent conversations, LLM gateway/budgets, plugin marketplace).
public_stack_signals: GitHub org renamed All-Hands-AI -> OpenHands (API redirect); main repo OpenHands/OpenHands now hosts Agent Canvas (README h1), MIT, TypeScript, ~89k stars.

setup_notes: npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas && agent-canvas (Node 24+, uv); runs agent-server directly on the host with full filesystem access.
Docker: docker run -it --rm -p 8000:8000 -v $HOME/.openhands:/home/openhands/.openhands -v $PROJECTS_PATH:/projects ghcr.io/openhands/agent-canvas:1.24.0; UI at /canvas.
From source: git clone OpenHands/OpenHands && npm install && npm run dev.
Desktop preview installers attached to GitHub releases (dmg/exe/AppImage/deb).
ACP guests require the guest CLI's own subscription login or API key; subscription login takes priority over an API key.
Settings, LLM config, MCP servers and automations are scoped to the active backend.

research.positioning: An open-source, self-hosted developer control center (Agent Canvas) for running coding agents and automations: the first-party, model-agnostic OpenHands agent by default, plus ACP guest agents, across local, Docker, VM, Kubernetes and OpenHands Cloud/Enterprise backends.

infrastructure: Default: full stack (frontend, agent server, automation, ingress) on the operator's machine; without Docker the agent has full host filesystem access.
Docker image or per-conversation Docker tool isolation provides sandboxed execution with mounted project directories.
Additional backends: remote Agent Servers on VMs, Mac Minis, Modal, Kubernetes (Helm), or OpenHands Cloud; one Canvas can switch between them.
LLM traffic goes to the user's configured provider (BYO key) or OpenHands LLM provider; ACP guests use their own CLI credentials.
Remote/mobile access via --public mode with API key, reverse proxy/TLS, or Tailscale/ngrok.

parity_risks: Hybrid runtime: record whether the run used the OpenHands agent or an ACP guest; guest runs measure the guest more than OpenHands.
OpenHands-agent results depend heavily on the chosen LLM; pin model and provider.
Docker mount paths (/projects) differ from host paths; verify on the actual worktree the agent edited.
npm path runs unsandboxed with host filesystem access; not equivalent to Docker-sandboxed runs.
Cloud/Enterprise runs (hosted sandboxes, integrations) are not parity-equivalent to local Class A runs.
Very fast release cadence (several minor releases per week); pin version.

hypotheses: Brand and community scale of the leading open-source coding agent project give distribution peers lack.
Owning a model-agnostic agent SDK plus Agent Server API lets them power CLI, Canvas, Cloud and third-party products from one engine.
Backend abstraction (laptop to Kubernetes to Cloud) plus automations positions it as an always-on agent team, not just a chat UI.
Commercial Enterprise (VPC, SSO, budgets, observability) funds the MIT core.
